primitives.name: Blocking the Punt
primitives.verbatim_quote: When the opponents punt, the center, working with the two guards, should break through and block the kick.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes linear offensive line formation, simultaneous action by three players, and opponent punter executing predictable trajectory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when defensive alignment disrupts the planned three-man breach, leading to failed block.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Models the probability of punt block success as a conformal prediction interval derived from historical defensive front performance against specific offensive formations.
layer2.telemetry: Observed punt return yardage differential between blocked and unblocked punts.

primitives.name: Quarterback Drop Back
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is better for the quarter to drop back from three to five yards behind his center, to watch out for "fake kicks" around the end or through the line.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes quarterback retreats three to five yards behind center to observe play progression and detect fake kicks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when quarterback drops too early or fails to recognize fakes, resulting in misread plays.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Treats quarterback drop depth as a hyperparameter in a sequential decision process, optimizing for minimal expected sack rate conditional on defensive pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Quarterback completion percentage adjusted for sacks and pressure events.

primitives.name: Halfback Plunge
primitives.verbatim_quote: The half back is called upon to make fierce plunges into the line and rapid dashes around the end.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes halfback follows optimal running lane dictated by blocking scheme, with velocity vector oriented toward maximum yardage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime where defensive line penetrates blocking assignment, causing sudden deceleration and loss of gained yardage.

layer2.mapping: GSE - Represents halfback plunge as a state-transition automaton where current ball-carrier position maps to next-yardage probability distributions conditioned on defensive front.
layer2.telemetry: Average yards per carry by halfback, segmented by defensive alignment.

primitives.name: Quick Eye Ability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each should have a quick eye and the ability to act on the instant as the situation demands.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes halfback must process visual information at 20-30 frames per second to identify cut blocks and adjust running path instantly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime where perceptual delay exceeds reaction time window, causing collision with defensive linemen.

layer2.mapping: GSE - Encodes quick-eye processing as a Kalman filter updating posterior distribution over defensive gaps, guiding real-time running lane selection.
layer2.telemetry: Halfback success rate in cutting blocks within 0.5 seconds of gap opening.
